properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/09/2025 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Somerset Township, Somerset county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/09/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8258395
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2025
Comments: On December 9, 2025, the Department conducted a Complaint Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County.At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at the time of this inspection. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a wellhead with a well tag fixed to it that had all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead. A small production tank was observed to be connected to the wellhead and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. A conductivity meter was utilized to screen the area around the right production tank as well as utilized to collect a background soil conductivity reading of 0.234 mS taken upslope and adjacent to the well site. A soil conductivity readings of 1.285 mS was collected below a corroded pipe, and then readings of 0.0089 mS and 0.0694 mS were collected downslope of this area. The reading taken below the corroded pipe is elevated when compared to background, subjugating that a release likely occurred here. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the broken corroded pipe near the top of the production tank and for a release from corroded piping on the production tank.

Comments: I arrived to the site at approximately 1100 hrs. The weather was warm and sunny with a slight breeze. The purpose of this inspection was to photograph the section of damaged casing that was removed from the well on 9/21/2023. Plugging activities were ongoing at the 9H gas well at the time of the inspection. Upon my arrival, I spoke with Brian Heffron (Repsol HSE) and then Repsol representative, Brad Campbell, who led me to the staging area for the damaged casing. At that time, I observed a section of 5 1/2" diameter casing approximately 13' in length, which included a 3' pup joint, attached to a casing hanger. I observed three (3) distinct holes located approximately 1 1/2' along the 3' pup joint, which was attached to the casing hanger. The dimensions of the holes ranged in size from approximately 1/8" to 2" and varied from a straight-lined crack to irregular and rounded in shape - see attached photos. Violations were previously cited on 8/28/2023 (Inspection Record #3611541) and 9/21/2023 (Inspection Record #3618680); these are continuing violations. No new violations were noted during this inspection. I left the location at approximately 1145 hrs.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 906383
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/01/2021
Comments: On January 29, 2021, Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported a spill of brine water to the DEP. The DEP spoke with Mr. Stevenson on February 1, 2021 to follow up with the reported spill. Beech Resources was in the process of pulling up their liner used for the recent stimulation of the new wells drilled and noticed staining on the pad surface. Mr. Stevenson estimated the volume of the spill to be about 1,500 gallons. The area of impact that was excavated is reported to be 100 ft. by 125 ft. and about 6 inches of the pad surface was removed. When DEP spoke with Mr. Stevenson on the phone, Beech Resources had finished excavating the impacted soil on Saturday January 30, 2021, and Penn E&R had collected confirmatory samples for the site. DEP was unable to complete an in person investigation due to the winter weather. DEP will follow up with a site inspection as soon as weather allows. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report No. 3139277.

Comments: 08/09/2023This administrative inspection is being conducted for the Ironman Well Site following violations issued on 07/18/2023 (IR: 3589336, Enf: 418538).Violations of 78a57(a), 78a66(b)1ii, 78a66(b)1i, 78a66(b)2, 91.33(A), 91.34(A), 78a54, and SWMA 301 were issued on 07/18/2023, following an incident inspection conducted in response to a spill report recieved by the Department on 07/17/2023. The following is required to be included within the 15 day report, however deficiencies were noted within, specifically A, D, E, and G: 78a.66. Reporting and remediating spills and releases. (c)(2)(i) Within 15 business days of the spill or release, the operator or other responsible party shall provide an initial written report that includes, to the extent that the information is available, the following:(A) The regulated substance involved.(B) The location where the spill or release occurred.(C) The environmental media affected.(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities.(F) Interim remedial actions planned, initiated or completed.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible partyintends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedulefor site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated timeframes within which it expects to take those actions.The following deficiencies were noted within the 15 Day Report submitted on 08/02/2023:(A) The regulated substance involved: EQT's report mentions leak from dump line, but does not specifically mention the regulated substance.(C) EQT's report did not mention an assessment of potential impact to Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).(D) Pollution or threatened pollution of water supplies: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(E) Impacts to buildings or utilities: Not mentioned in EQT's report.(G) A summary of the actions the operator or other responsible party intends to take at the site to address the spill or release such as a schedule for site characterization, to the extent known, and the anticipated time frames within which it expects to take those actions: EQT mentions entering Act 2, but provides no timeline. EQT indicates assessment will focus on dump line trench and northern pad slope, but does not discuss WOC.Due to the deficiencies noted within the 15 Day Report, a violation of 78a66(c)2i is being issued for the failure to provide a complete initial written report within 15 days. properties.content:

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8277564
Permit API: 123-47222
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. The bottom of the eroded channel was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Areas downslope of the tank battery where the flow of fluid was observed to widen (visible via the wide swath of stressed and dead vegetation) were observed to have elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 5,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The downslope path of the released fluid was then captured by a lease road ditch approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

The contractor (Bigler Boyz Environmental) began remediation of this site on 8/17/23. Three roll-off containers remain on-site. No soil sample documentation has been received by the Department as of this date, and heavy deer tracks at the restored site indicate that there may still be some residual contamination. Alldocumentation regarding the Act 2 clean-up of this site should be submitted to the Department as soon as it is available.The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The water in the southwest stormwater vault was about 6 feet from the top of the vault. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24 uS/cm. Seep 1, 1a, and 2 were dry and could not be screened. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 33.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 76.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Three monitoring wells have been drilled about 50 yards to the west of the well pad. All the infiltration berms at the site have been hydro seeded. The percent vegetated cover varies from berm to berm. Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Sweden Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-22
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCDT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 106 Well Pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 1/22/2019 @1130 hours. The weather was 16 degrees, overcast, winds S@9mph. Approximately 12" of snow was deposited onsite in the previous 72 hours. JKLM representative Scott West and DEP Env Trainee, Korey Starkey was present onsite. JKLM contractor Pro Frac is currently stimulating the 6 utica wells onsite. Mr. West stated at the time of this inspection they had just completed stimulating stage 13 of the 2HU well, and perforating stage 7 of the 5HU well. Two small spills have been reported within the last week on the SV 106 well site, during the frack. Spill #1 (CTS#339324), occurred and was reported on 1/16/2019. The spill reportedly involved the release of 400 to 500 gallons of brine from the working tank. The spill was reportedly mostly on primary containment with some spray hitting the perimeter of the pad. As of today's inspection the secondary containment around the working tanks was full of snow. One area in the containment, which appeared to be a high foot traffic area, had slush/fluid mix with a field measure conductivity of "Over Range". A vac truck was dispatched to remove the fluid. The containment had recently been repaired in the same area. No melted slush or fluid was observed outside of containment. Additional screening, when conditions allow, under and around the secondary containment was discussed with a representative from Whipper Hill Consulting while onsite. Spill #2 (CTS#339357), occurred and was reported on 1/18/2019. This spill involved the reported release of a few hundred gallons of produced water into containment from a pump filter. The containment berm was compressed allowing 20-30 gallons of produced water to leave the containment impacting the pad surface. As of today's inspection the area along the perimeter of the compromised containment where the spill occurred was snow covered. No melted or stained areas were observed. An onsite representative from Whipper Hill Consulting provided grid drawings of pre and post excavation soil conductivity readings of the impacted area. The highest recorded soil conductivity reading was 1.44mS/cm, the remaining readings were <1.0mS/cm. Excavated materials were placed in waste containers and staged inside containment awaiting disposal. Violations of 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(B) and SWMA 301 are cited as Immediate Corrected at this time. Please address any deficiencies noted and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1300 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 369324

Comments: On 9/12/2024, the Department received a call regarding a bubbling hole located in the vicinity of the above-referenced gas well. During this inspection, fluid with a sheen is observed within tertiary containment outside the OBM tanks. Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, routine inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources Inc well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on April 1, 2016.The following was observed:Well 10H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 1 and 2). A small amount of grease was observed on the well pad surface below the well head (see photo 3). There are five other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 4). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). Additional secondary containment that appeared to be severely deteriorated was observed next to the production tanks (see photo 6). This appears to be used for pump trucks that empty the production tanks. The ERP and PPC plan were onsite (see photos 7 and 8). Deep accelerated erosion rills were observed in multiple portions of the access road, with one of them appearing to empty into a storm culvert (see photos 11-15). The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that any grease or other fluids used during routine maintenance that fall onto the well pad surface are immediately removed. The Department also recommends that deteriorated secondary containments and other onsite equipment are replaced to mitigate the risk of a spill from occurring on site. Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:31 in response to a reported release of 15 gallons of glycol from a compressor. I talked with Kellon Balum, Chief, during the inspection. The area can then be backfilled and the residual waste disposed of properly. The DEP acknowledges the proper reporting and prompt remediation of the release. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted & Immediately Corrected.

Comments: On September 18 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504. The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504.No E and S Plan was found on site. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 838325

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-07
Comments: On January 7, 2019, Department representatives Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of the reported spill on PGE Company LLC. Moore Rd. Ext. The Department met Chris Earley and Chad Oechler with PGE. A tanker truck was hauling production fluids from COP Tract 729 Pad E, as the truck was driving down the access road a valve failed on the tank. This caused about 2-3 barrels of production fluid to spill on Moore Rd. Ext. The tanker truck also spilled about 10 gallons on COP Tract 729 Pad E. At the time of the investigation, the soil could be seen stained about 40 yds x 15 yds. Specific conductivity measurements were taken in the area of the affected soil with a range of 2.1 mS/cm to 4.0 mS/cm. 4.0 mS/cm is the upper limit of the Department's meter. Specific conductivity was also measured in UNT to Ramsey with a reading of 25.2 uS/cm. UNT to Ramsey run pH measured 7.6. At the time of the measurements, UNT to Ramsey Run appeared unaffected by the spill. PGE had a contractor there removing the contaminated soil with Moody and Associates delineating the spill area on Moore Rd. Ext. The contaminated soil was excavated off Pad E and placed on plastic to be loaded in a roll back dumpster. The release of production fluid is considered a violation since the estimated volume is over 42 gallons. PGE is required to go through the Act 2 process.
